sources.label: Roblox Creator Hub: What is Roblox?
Roblox Creator Hub: Publishing games and places

coverage.scopeNote: All terms in the current RobloxDen and official Roblox dictionaries are represented as cards or deduplicated aliases, then expanded with official creator documentation and established community sources.

items.definition: A fair match where two players compete against each other, often in a fight or skill challenge.
items.example: They joined a private server for a 1v1 after the match ended.

items.definition: An older Roblox age label used to show that content or a feature was aimed at users aged 13 or over. Current access labels can differ, so treat it as historical context rather than a promise of access.
items.example: The old guide marked the feature 13+, but the player checked the current Roblox settings instead.
items.safetyNote: Age and access labels change. Check the current Roblox screen or help page instead of relying on an old label.

items.definition: Older gamer slang for elite skill or style, written with numbers that resemble letters.
items.example: The winner typed 1337 after the round as a deliberately old-school flex.

items.definition: Trading shorthand asking whether someone will accept the offer or send a counteroffer.
items.example: The trader posted A/C after sending a limited-item offer.
items.safetyNote: Use Roblox's official trade window and review every item before accepting.

items.definition: Trading shorthand asking whether an offer should be accepted or declined.
items.example: She asked A/D before deciding whether the trade was fair.
items.safetyNote: Do not let chat pressure rush a trade decision.

items.definition: Admin abuse is when an experience administrator misuses special commands or powers to disrupt play or treat players unfairly.
items.example: Players called it AA when an admin repeatedly kicked people who won a round.

items.definition: A Roblox chat response used to show interest in a request or roleplay prompt, such as an offer to team up or take a role.
items.example: Someone typed ABC for cashier, and two players replied ABC.
items.safetyNote: Replying ABC does not create a real agreement. Keep personal details and off-platform contact out of roleplay chats.

items.definition: Your Roblox login profile that holds your avatar, inventory, friends, and game progress.
items.example: She signed into her account before joining the group game night.
items.safetyNote: Never share your password, 2-step codes, or login links. Roblox staff will not ask for your password in chat or messages.

items.definition: Extra conditions that apply on top of Roblox's main User Terms, Creator Terms, Community Standards, privacy materials, and regional rules when you use certain features or products.
items.example: A limited-time event may list Additional Terms that players must accept before joining.

items.definition: A player with special powers in a game or group, such as kicking users or changing server settings.
items.example: The admin muted chat so everyone could hear the event announcement.

items.definition: Roblox plus the people and companies linked to it, including officers, directors, employees, consultants, affiliates, investors, partners, subsidiaries, and agents named together in the Terms.
items.example: Liability sections often protect Roblox and its Affiliated Parties from certain claims.

items.definition: A short way to say you stepped away and are not actively playing right now.
items.example: He typed AFK and left his avatar standing near the lobby fountain.

items.definition: An older friend feature that let a player privately assign a nickname to someone on their Roblox friends list.
items.example: The old account guide showed how a friend alias appeared only to the person who set it.

items.definition: A casual chat reply meaning okay, understood, or that a plan works.
items.example: ALR, meet the squad beside spawn.

items.definition: A second Roblox account someone uses in addition to their main one.
items.example: She used an alt to test the new game without spoiling her main inventory.

items.definition: A right a creator grants Roblox to use that creator's UGC when marketing or advertising Roblox and its services.
items.example: Roblox may rely on Ancillary Use rights when featuring creator content in promotional material.

items.definition: A saved sequence of poses that makes an avatar, character, or rig move.
items.example: The animator published a new run animation for the enemy rig.

items.definition: Once per year. On a Roblox purchase or subscription screen, it describes how often a recurring charge is scheduled.
items.example: The player checked whether the plan billed monthly or annually before choosing it.
items.safetyNote: Confirm the amount and renewal schedule on the current purchase screen before paying.

items.definition: A roleplay status telling law-enforcement characters to arrest a named character when seen.
items.example: The suspect became AOS after escaping the roleplay jail.

items.definition: The official Roblox mobile application that players install on phones and tablets to access experiences, avatars, chat, and account features.
items.example: A player opened the App on their phone to join an experience.

items.definition: A formal request asking Roblox to recheck a suspension, account termination, or removal of UGC or Virtual Content that followed a Terms violation decision.
items.example: After a moderation ban, you submit an Appeal explaining why the action was incorrect.

items.definition: A U.S. User Terms clause that sends unresolved disputes to binding individual arbitration and waives jury trials and class-action style proceedings.
items.example: The Arbitration Agreement section explains how U.S. users resolve most legal disputes with Roblox.

items.definition: A piece of content on Roblox such as clothing, a model, a sound, or an image used in experiences.
items.example: The creator uploaded a new asset for the shop’s window display.

items.definition: The unique number Roblox assigns to an asset such as an image, model, audio file, or animation.
items.example: The creator pasted the asset ID into the property that loads the image.

items.definition: A Roblox Studio window for importing and managing assets tied to the current project.
items.example: The creator used Asset Manager to upload the new lobby image.

items.definition: A sound or music asset that a Roblox game can load and play through its audio objects.
items.example: The button played a short audio clip when the round began.

items.definition: A cool look, style, or presence a player seems to have in chat or gameplay, often as a joke compliment.
items.example: After the clutch win, the chat said his aura was unmatched.

items.definition: The character you control on Roblox, including your body type, clothes, and accessories.
items.example: She changed her avatar’s jacket before joining the fashion runway game.

items.definition: A nickname for the classic Pal Hair look that appeared on many default Roblox avatars.
items.example: The group photo mixed a bacon-style avatar with several custom outfits.

items.definition: A reward icon a game can give you for finishing a goal, finding a secret, or hitting a milestone.
items.example: He earned a badge for completing the beginner parkour course.

items.definition: A penalty that blocks a player from Roblox or from a specific game for breaking the rules.
items.example: The account got a ban after repeated chat violations in the lobby.
items.safetyNote: A ban is a safety and rules action. Do not try to dodge it with extra accounts, and never trust anyone who claims they can remove a ban for payment or free items.

items.definition: Slang for losing an account or valuable items because of account theft or a deceptive link.
items.example: He said his account got beamed after he clicked a fake free-item message.
items.safetyNote: If someone says you got beamed, treat it as a warning about theft. Do not click unknown login links, and tell a trusted adult if your account or items go missing.

items.definition: An early test version of a game or feature that is still being improved before a wider release.
items.example: Players in the beta could try the new map a week early.

items.definition: An avatar look built from simple rectangular body parts, similar to the classic Roblox character shape.
items.example: The outfit used a blocky body with modern layered accessories.

items.definition: Classic Roblox slang for defeating or knocking out another player in older combat games.
items.example: In the classic arena, the winner proudly said the rival had been bloxxed.

items.definition: A joke misspelling of Robux used in memes, chat, and playful requests for currency.
items.example: The sign promised free bobux, but the player ignored the suspicious claim.
items.safetyNote: Free-Robux promises are a common scam lure. Do not enter login details on unknown sites.

items.definition: A chat phrase meaning you will step away for a short time and return soon.
items.example: She typed BRB and paused the trade until she came back.

items.definition: An early Roblox combat style that used classic tools like rockets, bombs, and swords in blocky arenas.
items.example: Their favorite classic place was a BrickBattle map with team bases.

items.definition: A change that makes a character, item, or ability stronger than it was before.
items.example: The update gave the starter sword a small damage buff.

items.definition: A Marketplace listing that groups a complete avatar body or a set of related avatar parts under one item.
items.example: She equipped a robot bundle, then mixed its arms with a different avatar body.

items.definition: An unsafe attempt to get around Roblox chat filters or other safety protections.
items.example: The moderator removed players who tried to use a bypass in public chat.
items.safetyNote: Bypass talk is not allowed and can lead to reports or bans. If you see someone trying to hide unsafe messages, leave the chat and report the behavior.

items.definition: Slang for a false claim or exaggeration. Players say no cap when they mean they are telling the truth.
items.example: That trade offer is cap; the item is not that rare.

items.definition: When a strong teammate does most of the work so the rest of the team still wins.
items.example: Our tank carried the round while we finished the objective.

items.definition: Converting eligible Earned Robux into U.S. dollars through DevEx, using the program's rules and the exchange rate in effect at payout.
items.example: Once approved for DevEx, a developer can Cash Out qualifying Robux each payout window.

items.definition: Roblox systems that hide or block chat text that breaks the rules or is not allowed for a player's age settings.
items.example: The chat filter replaced some of her message with hashtags.

items.definition: Context-dependent chat slang that may be a playful spelling of chill or child. The surrounding sentence decides which meaning fits.
items.example: Chile, it was one missed jump, not the end of the obby.

aliases: Shenzhen Tencent Computer Systems Co., Ltd.
items.definition: Shenzhen Tencent Computer Systems Co., Ltd., the company named as publisher and operator partner for Roblox-related services in China.
items.example: Regional notices may name the China Publisher when describing the PRC version of the platform.

items.definition: Roblox-made avatar body models that creators may license and use on the platform under the Creator Terms when building experiences or content.
items.example: Studio tutorials often start from a Classic Avatar before you customize clothing and proportions.

items.definition: Older style avatar outfits that use flat shirt, pants, and related layers instead of layered 3D clothing.
items.example: He wore classic clothing with a simple T-shirt template.

items.definition: A Roblox space creators can own and manage to connect with audiences, share updates, showcase experiences, and host discussions. Communities replaced the public Groups name.
items.example: The creator posted an experience update in the Community for its players.

items.definition: Slang for being completely outplayed, embarrassed, or left with no good options in a match.
items.example: We got cooked in the final round of the tower defense map.

items.definition: Roblox avatar slang for a recognizable outfit style that uses many of the same body shapes, faces, hairstyles, and accessories as other players.
items.example: Their matching copy-and-paste avatars used similar hair, faces, and dark outfits.

items.definition: A person who builds experiences, avatars, items, or other content on Roblox.
items.example: The creator posted a new update for the racing experience.

items.definition: Roblox's web workspace for managing games, places, assets, analytics, access, and creator settings.
items.example: The developer opened Creator Dashboard to review the game's places and permissions.

items.definition: A Roblox bonus program that pays eligible experience creators for daily player engagement and growth of their audience under program rules.
items.example: Strong daily visits can qualify an experience for Creator Rewards payouts.

items.definition: The Roblox marketplace where creators browse, share, and use models, plugins, audio, and other development assets.
items.example: She found a free park bench model in the Creator Store.

items.definition: The contract rules for creators using Studio and creating, publishing, monetizing, and managing Virtual Content, music, and related creator activity on Roblox.
items.example: Before enabling paid access, review the Creator Terms on monetization and UGC rights.

items.definition: Roleplay centered on structured fights and character actions during combat scenes.
items.example: The server rules asked players to agree before starting CRP.

items.definition: A Roblox cloud service creators use to save information that should persist between play sessions.
items.example: The game stored the player's unlocked tools in a DataStore.

items.definition: Older Roblox slang for a word placed near numbers in an attempt to get around chat filtering.
items.example: The moderator treated Dec followed by hidden numbers as a filter-bypass attempt.
items.safetyNote: Do not use coded prefixes to bypass chat filters or share private numbers.

items.definition: The unique number that identifies a decal image asset so creators can apply that image in Studio or on items.
items.example: He pasted the Decal ID into the texture property of the sign.

items.definition: Short for developer, meaning someone who scripts, builds, or maintains a Roblox experience.
items.example: A dev fixed the bug that blocked the lobby door.

items.definition: A creator who designs, codes, or publishes Roblox experiences and related systems.
items.example: The developer added a daily quest board after the update.

items.definition: A creator-set purchase that players can buy more than once inside a Roblox game, unlike a one-time pass.
items.example: The revive button used a developer product because a player could purchase another revive later.
items.safetyNote: Check the current purchase prompt before spending Robux.

items.definition: Roblox's Developer Exchange Program, which lets eligible creators Cash Out Earned Robux for real-world currency under the DevEx Terms.
items.example: The developer reviewed the DevEx requirements before requesting a Cash Out.

items.definition: The conditions a creator must satisfy before exchanging Earned Robux for cash through the Developer Exchange program.
items.example: A creator checks the DevEx Eligibility Requirements before requesting a Cash Out.

items.definition: The full set of rules, policies, rates, requirements, and limits that control how Developer Exchange cash-outs work.
items.example: DevEx Terms list which Robux counts and what documentation creators must provide.

items.definition: Shorthand some players use for Discord or another off-platform chat server.
items.example: A stranger asked for her disc, so she kept the conversation on Roblox and left.
items.safetyNote: Do not move a conversation off Roblox because someone pressures you. Never share personal contact details with strangers.

items.definition: The name shown for a Roblox account in many social and in-game surfaces. It is separate from the account's unique username.
items.example: Her display name changed, but friends could still find the same username.
items.safetyNote: A familiar display name does not prove who controls an account. Check the username when identity matters.

items.definition: Any claim, controversy, or disagreement that relates to the Roblox Terms or your use of the platform.
items.example: Billing problems and account actions can become a Dispute under the User Terms.

items.definition: A private chat between players instead of public experience chat.
items.example: She sent a DM to invite her friend to the same server.

items.definition: Slang for a stylish avatar outfit or cool clothing combo.
items.example: His limited jacket and shoes gave him serious drip.

items.definition: A quick chat reply used to reassure someone that a mistake or delay is fine.
items.example: DW, we can restart the round if you disconnect.

items.definition: A text face used to show boredom, tiredness, or an unimpressed reaction.
items.example: The queue reset again, and chat answered e.e.

items.definition: Robux a creator legitimately earns from approved monetization of their content, not ordinary purchases, membership grants, or trading profits from reselling others' items.
items.example: Game passes sales that follow the rules count as Earned Robux for DevEx.

items.definition: A short avatar animation or dance players can trigger to react or show off in an experience.
items.example: After the win, the whole team played the same emote.

items.definition: A Roblox game or interactive project that players can join. Creator tools also use game and place, and one project can contain one or more places.
items.example: The project has a lobby place and two match places inside the same Roblox experience.

items.definition: Custom behavior rules set and enforced by an experience's creator for players inside that specific game, separate from platform-wide Community Standards.
items.example: The lobby posts Experience Rules banning griefing and requiring respectful team chat.

items.definition: A player who uses unauthorized tools or methods to gain unfair advantages and break normal game rules.
items.example: The server kicked an exploiter who moved faster than any normal character.
items.safetyNote: If you see unfair cheating behavior, leave the server if needed and report it through official Roblox tools. Do not try to copy or learn those methods.

items.definition: A boast claiming a match was easy, often typed after a win and sometimes seen as poor sportsmanship.
items.example: The winner typed EZ, while the rest of the lobby moved on to the rematch.

items.definition: A game model that lets players join without paying, though optional purchases may still exist.
items.example: The popular simulator is F2P, so anyone can start with the free tools.

items.definition: The U.S. Federal Arbitration Act, the federal statute that governs how the Arbitration Agreement operates for covered disputes.
items.example: The User Terms cite the FAA when describing how arbitration awards are enforced.

items.definition: A legacy Studio term for server-authoritative behavior that stopped ordinary client changes from automatically appearing for everyone.
items.example: An older scripting tutorial says the game is FE, even though filtering is now part of normal Roblox architecture.

items.definition: A national alternative-dispute-resolution organization that Roblox designates to run arbitration cases under its mandatory informal dispute process.
items.example: If MIDR fails, the Terms may send the case to FedArb for arbitration.

items.definition: A match mode where every player competes alone instead of joining fixed teams.
items.example: The sword arena switched to FFA for the final five minutes.

items.definition: A frustrated chat reaction whose full phrase usually contains profanity.
items.example: After the checkpoint failed again, the player typed FFS and took a break.
items.safetyNote: The expanded phrase may be inappropriate for Roblox chat. Use a calmer reaction instead.

items.definition: Showing off a rare avatar item, high stats, or a strong loadout so other players notice.
items.example: They joined the lobby just to flex their Limited wings.

items.definition: How many frames your device draws each second in a Roblox experience. Higher FPS usually feels smoother.
items.example: Turning down graphics helped my FPS stay steady in a crowded server.

items.definition: Roleplay slang for an unrealistic action that ignores the scene, breaks character, or goes against an experience's roleplay rules.
items.example: Driving away after a serious crash without reacting was marked as FRP by the server moderator.

items.definition: A one-time Robux purchase that grants a lasting privilege or unlock inside a Roblox game, as defined by its creator.
items.example: The Game Pass permanently unlocked an extra inventory slot for that game.

items.definition: A Roblox tool asset that players can equip or use in games that support it. Many classic games used catalog Gear heavily.
items.example: The classic arena allowed a sword Gear item, while the newer map disabled outside tools.

items.definition: Custom Roblox art such as thumbnails, logos, or renders made for games, groups, or profiles.
items.example: The developer hired an artist to make new GFX for the game icon.

items.definition: A short sportsmanlike message players send after a match or round ends.
items.example: Both teams typed GG in chat when the round finished.

items.definition: Repeating the same tasks, rounds, or farms to earn currency, levels, or items over time.
items.example: They planned to grind quests all afternoon for enough coins to buy the sword.

items.definition: The former public name for a Community. In Roblox's Creator Economic Terms, Group also means creators joined to release an Experience or other Virtual Content.
items.example: A creator team can publish through a Group while players see its public space as a Community.

items.definition: A parent or legal guardian responsible for a minor who uses Roblox and may need to consent to certain account actions.
items.example: A Guardian can help a child set privacy controls and recover account access.

items.definition: The on-screen interface players use, such as menus, buttons, health bars, and inventory panels.
items.example: The mobile GUI moved its jump button away from the shop panel.

items.definition: A senior role or member in a Roblox community or structured roleplay group.
items.example: An HR ran the training and reviewed the new recruits.

items.definition: A Roblox object that gives a character common behavior such as health, movement states, and name display.
items.example: The NPC needed a Humanoid so it could walk and take damage.

items.definition: Acting and chatting as your roleplay character instead of as yourself outside the story.
items.example: She stayed IC as the shopkeeper while customers entered the cafe.

items.definition: A quick reply meaning you are unsure about something another player asked.
items.example: When asked where the boss spawned, they answered IDK.

items.definition: A 2D asset used for interface graphics, textures, decals, thumbnails, and other visual surfaces on Roblox.
items.example: The inventory slot used an image asset for the potion icon.

items.definition: User-generated content that players obtain and use only inside a specific experience, such as game passes or special abilities.
items.example: Buying a speed boost pass unlocks In-Experience Items that work only in that game.

items.definition: Any object in Roblox's data model, including parts, scripts, folders, sounds, and interface elements.
items.example: The creator selected an instance in Explorer and changed its properties.

items.definition: Chat slang for a loss, bad outcome, or light criticism. Players say someone took an L after a failed match, trade, or choice.
items.example: We took an L in the finals, but the rematch is tomorrow.

items.definition: Avatar clothing that can stack and wrap over body shapes so jackets, shirts, and pants sit more naturally together.
items.example: Layered clothing let the jacket sit over the shirt without clipping as much.

items.definition: A dated, playful variation of LOL used as a light or sarcastic laugh.
items.example: He missed the easiest jump and typed lel before respawning.

items.definition: Audio recordings, compositions, or sound effects that Roblox licenses from third parties so creators can use them inside experiences on the platform.
items.example: A creator checks the license before adding Licensed Music to an experience.

items.definition: An avatar item marked Limited whose copies can be resold through supported Roblox systems. Classic and creator-made Limited items can follow different rules.
items.example: The player checked the Limited listing and recent sales before considering a resale.

items.definition: An older Roblox label for a Limited item released in a fixed quantity with numbered copies. Newer Limited systems may use different labels and rules.
items.example: The archived item page called the numbered hat Limited Unique.

items.definition: The name of Roblox's retired trading forum, where players discussed Limited items, values, and possible deals.
items.example: Older trading guides may mention LMaD when describing how Limited traders compared offers.

items.definition: A strong laugh reaction whose full phrase contains profanity.
items.example: The cart rolled backward into the lobby and chat filled with LMAO.
items.safetyNote: Keep the meaning in mind before using it in spaces where profanity is not appropriate.

items.definition: A Luau code container that runs on a player's device for local input, camera, interface, and similar client behavior.
items.example: The LocalScript opened the inventory when the player pressed the key.

items.definition: A common chat reaction that means you found something funny.
items.example: The fail montage was so silly that half the server spammed LOL.

items.definition: The programming language used to script Roblox experiences. It is based on Lua with Roblox-specific features.
items.example: They wrote the shop script in Luau inside Roblox Studio.

items.definition: The PRC-operated edition of Roblox Studio used to build UGC for Roblox services and the Luobulesi Game.
items.example: Creators in China publish experiences with Luobu Studio for the local platform version.

items.definition: The Roblox platform version operated for players in the People's Republic of China under local publishing arrangements.
items.example: Accounts on the Luobulesi Game follow regional rules set for PRC users.

items.definition: Number-based chat slang for mate, meaning a friend or another player.
items.example: Nice save, m8, you kept the whole team alive.

items.definition: Your primary Roblox account, character slot, or most-used setup, as opposed to an alternate one.
items.example: He keeps rare items on his main and uses an alt for testing games.

items.definition: The Roblox storefront where players browse and buy avatar items, including clothes, accessories, and other creations.
items.example: She found a new jacket in the Marketplace and added it to her avatar.

items.definition: A custom 3D shape used to give a Roblox object more detail than basic block parts.
items.example: The sword blade used an imported mesh while its handle stayed a simple part.

items.definition: The strategies, classes, or items players currently treat as strongest or most common in a game.
items.example: After the balance update, the meta shifted away from heavy tanks.

items.definition: A phrase inviting or challenging another player to talk through voice chat instead of typing.
items.example: Someone typed mic up after the match, but she chose to keep the conversation in public chat.
items.safetyNote: You never have to join voice chat. Mute, block, or report anyone who pressures you or makes the conversation unsafe.

items.definition: Mandatory Informal Dispute Resolution, the required pre-arbitration steps in the User Terms for trying to resolve a dispute with Roblox before formal arbitration.
items.example: The User Terms describe MIDR as a step before covered disputes proceed to arbitration.

items.definition: A user who is under the legal age of majority in the place where they live, so extra consent and safety rules may apply.
items.example: A Minor may need Guardian permission before making certain purchases or sharing data.

items.definition: A quick chat reply meaning okay or understood.
items.example: Meet at spawn after the round. MK.

items.definition: Older gaming slang for a highly skilled or exaggerated highlight play, often used sarcastically.
items.example: The lucky trick shot got called MLG in the replay chat.

items.definition: A player or staff member who helps keep a game fair by enforcing rules and handling reports.
items.example: A mod muted chat after players started spamming the lobby.

items.definition: A container that groups parts, meshes, scripts, or other Roblox objects into one reusable build.
items.example: The shop model contained the walls, counter, signs, and door script.
items.safetyNote: Review unfamiliar models before using them, especially when they contain scripts.

items.definition: A Classic Avatar that a creator has altered or customized under the Creator Terms while still using Roblox's licensed base model.
items.example: A creator customized a Classic Avatar under the rules for a Modified Classic Avatar.

items.definition: A reusable Luau code container that returns values or functions for other scripts to use.
items.example: Both shop scripts required the same ModuleScript for price formatting.

items.definition: A middle-level role in a Roblox community or structured roleplay group, below its high ranks and above entry roles.
items.example: The new MR helped train members but could not change the top roles.

items.definition: Original music compositions written or owned by a creator, either alone or with collaborators, separate from third-party Licensed Music.
items.example: Uploading your own song means you control the Musical Works rights in that composition.

items.definition: A legacy label for a player who did not have Builders Club under Roblox's retired membership system.
items.example: The old forum post compared NBC accounts with the three Builders Club tiers.

items.definition: A balance change that makes a weapon, ability, or item weaker so it is less dominant in play.
items.example: After the update nerf, that sword no longer one-shots most players.

items.definition: A polite way to describe a new or less experienced player who is still learning the game.
items.example: He is a newb at tower defense, so the team walked him through the first few waves.

items.definition: A sometimes dismissive label for a newer or younger player who missed an earlier era of a game or Roblox culture.
items.example: Calling every new player a newgen did not help them learn the map.
items.safetyNote: The term can be insulting. Explain the reference instead of using it to exclude newer players.

items.definition: In Roblox trading, a label saying the owner is not offering an item. Outside that context, NFT can mean non-fungible token.
items.example: The limited stayed NFT because it was part of the owner's main outfit.

items.definition: A claim used in unofficial deals to say the speaker will not send their item or currency first.
items.example: The stranger insisted on NGF during an off-platform deal, so the player left.
items.safetyNote: NGF pressure is a scam warning. Avoid unofficial and cross-platform deals, and use Roblox's supported purchase or trade systems.

items.definition: Chat slang meaning a player is telling the truth and not exaggerating.
items.example: No cap, that limited sold out in under a minute on the catalog.

items.definition: A common label for a new or unskilled player. It can sound rude, so many players prefer friendlier wording.
items.example: Calling someone a noob after one loss is usually just trash talk, not real skill talk.

items.definition: A character controlled by the game, not by a real player, often used for quests, shops, or story scenes.
items.example: Talk to the shop NPC near the spawn pad to buy better tools.

items.definition: A short chat reply that politely turns down a trade, invite, or offer.
items.example: NTY, I am saving my Robux for a game pass later.

items.definition: A quick way to cancel an earlier question or say the issue no longer matters.
items.example: NVM, I found the quest NPC beside spawn.

items.definition: A Roblox experience built around jumping, timing, and parkour challenges from stage to stage.
items.example: That free obby has 200 stages and a finish line reward at the end.

items.definition: The highest tier of Roblox's retired Builders Club membership.
items.example: The classic profile screenshot shows an OBC badge beside the username.

items.definition: A context-dependent term. Older chat references may mean a replacement shown for an unsupported character, while creators use OBJ for a common 3D model file format.
items.example: The creator asked for the OBJ file, not the odd obj symbol that appeared in chat.

items.definition: A player who uses Roblox mainly to seek romantic chat or dating-style attention instead of normal gameplay.
items.example: If someone asks personal questions in a hangout game, they may be acting like an ODer.
items.safetyNote: Do not share personal details, and do not move chats off Roblox. Leave or report if someone pushes for private contact.

items.definition: Chat shorthand for an obvious yes or a confident confirmation.
items.example: OFC I will join after this round ends.

items.definition: A chat reaction showing surprise, excitement, or disbelief. OML is a common variation.
items.example: OMG, the rare pet dropped on the first try.

items.definition: A dated variation of OMG used to show surprise or added to a username for style.
items.example: The old chat log says OMQ after the rare item drops.

items.definition: A roleplay label for a message spoken as the player rather than as the character they are acting.
items.example: OOC, I need to leave the server for a minute.

items.definition: The name of Roblox's former classic death sound, now also used as a short reaction when something goes wrong.
items.example: He missed the final jump and typed oof before trying the obby again.

items.definition: A note that a message or subject is outside the current game or roleplay scene.
items.example: The event schedule is OOG, so the characters would not discuss it in the scene.

items.definition: In gameplay, something far stronger than normal options. Context can change the meaning, such as original poster in forum threads.
items.example: That pet feels OP because it doubles coin gains for the whole party.

items.definition: A limited license from Roblox that lets creators use Other Roblox Content together with their own UGC on the platform.
items.example: A creator reviews the Other Content License before using Roblox-provided content in UGC.

items.definition: Content created by Roblox and offered to creators for use, not including Classic Avatars or Modified Classic Avatars.
items.example: The Creator Terms distinguish Other Roblox Content from Classic Avatar models.

items.definition: The person or organization chosen to represent a Community, manage its registration email, and act on its behalf on Roblox.
items.example: A Community notice may identify the Owner who represents it on Roblox.

items.definition: A label for an experience where spending Robux on upgrades gives a strong gameplay advantage over players who do not pay.
items.example: Players called the arena P2W because its strongest weapon was available only through a paid upgrade.

items.definition: A reusable Roblox asset or object hierarchy whose copies can receive updates from the same source.
items.example: The team used one door package across several maps so fixes stayed consistent.

items.definition: A Roblox game or experience that requires a Robux purchase before a player can join it.
items.example: The join screen showed Paid Access, so the player checked the purchase before continuing.
items.safetyNote: Review the current purchase screen before spending Robux.

items.definition: A basic 3D object used to build Roblox worlds, such as a block, sphere, wedge, or cylinder.
items.example: The builder resized a part into a platform and anchored it above the lava.

items.definition: A joke aimed at someone who bought a paid advantage but still lost to players without it.
items.example: The expensive weapon missed every shot, and chat called it pay to lose.

items.definition: A published Roblox world or level that players can join. Experiences can include one or more places linked together.
items.example: The creator added a tutorial place before the main battle map.

items.definition: A playful, dated spelling of please that appeared in older Roblox and gaming chat.
items.example: Open the gate plox, the round is about to start.

items.definition: An extension that adds tools or workflows to Roblox Studio.
items.example: The builder used a plugin to align a row of parts evenly.
items.safetyNote: Install plugins only from sources you trust and review the permissions or behavior they add.

items.definition: The People's Republic of China, the region referenced for local platform versions, publishers, and related operating rules.
items.example: Luobu and Luobulesi materials apply specifically to users and creators in the PRC.

items.definition: Roblox's paid membership program, which provides a Robux allowance and other platform benefits that can change over time.
items.example: She checked the current Premium benefits before deciding whether the membership suited her account.

items.definition: The policy that explains what information Roblox collects, how it is protected and used, and how it fits into the User Terms.
items.example: Before creating an account, review the Privacy Policy for data collection practices.

items.definition: A separate server instance whose owner can control who joins. An experience can offer private servers for free or for Robux.
items.example: They opened a private server so their group could practice the raid without a crowded lobby.

items.definition: A Performing Rights Organization that represents musical works and helps collect public-performance royalties for copyright holders.
items.example: Songwriters often register compositions with a PRO so venues and platforms report usage.

items.definition: A request to speak used in structured military, training, and similar Roblox roleplay communities.
items.example: The recruit typed PTS before asking the trainer a question.

items.definition: Releasing UGC on Roblox by creating, uploading, submitting, displaying, generating, transmitting, or otherwise making it available to others.
items.example: A creator chooses Publish when making new UGC available through Roblox.

items.definition: Older gamer slang for completely beating someone, often used after a decisive win in chat or matches.
items.example: Back then, typing pwned after a clean 1v1 win was common in classic fighting places.

items.definition: Chat shorthand for cutie, usually used as a light compliment.
items.example: The matching avatar outfits looked qt in the group photo.
items.safetyNote: Keep compliments respectful and stop if another player is uncomfortable.

items.definition: A classic Roblox avatar body type with six main parts and simpler joint movement than newer rigs.
items.example: Some older games still force R6 so classic animations and hitboxes stay consistent.

items.definition: A modern Roblox avatar body type with fifteen parts, allowing more natural animations and body scaling.
items.example: Most new experiences support R15 so avatars can use smoother walk and emote animations.

items.definition: A Virtual Item obtained inside an experience through a randomized acquisition system rather than a fixed, direct purchase of that exact item.
items.example: Opening a mystery crate can grant a Random Virtual Item from a prize pool.

items.definition: A position in a Roblox Community hierarchy, or a competitive level inside a game when the context is ranked play.
items.example: Her community rank allowed training new members, while her arena rank tracked match skill.

items.definition: The recent average sale price shown for limited marketplace items, used as a rough market value guide.
items.example: Traders check RAP before offering a limited hat so the trade values look fair.

items.definition: In combat experiences, RDM means harming another player for no valid match reason, such as outside the role, rule set, or objective.
items.example: The admin warned the team that RDM would get someone removed from the roleplay server.

items.definition: A drawn-out text scream used for exaggerated frustration or a joking meltdown.
items.example: The moving platform reset at the finish, and chat answered REEEE.

items.definition: A Roblox object used to send one-way messages between client and server scripts.
items.example: The LocalScript fired a RemoteEvent, and the server checked the request before changing the score.

items.definition: When Premium or Plus members sell eligible Roblox-created Virtual Content again through Roblox marketplace tools under platform resale rules.
items.example: Limited items support Resale so eligible members can list them on the marketplace.

items.definition: A character model with joints and structure prepared for posing and animation.
items.example: The animator loaded an R15 rig before creating the emote.

items.definition: Attacking or defeating another player without a valid roleplay or match reason, similar to RDM.
items.example: The roleplay moderator warned the player for RK outside the combat scene.

items.definition: RNG is the luck factor behind random outcomes in Roblox games, such as item rolls, crit chance, or loot drops.
items.example: They kept fishing because good RNG can still give a rare catch on the next try.

items.definition: Roblox Corporation and the subsidiaries identified in the Roblox Terms as the companies operating the platform and related services.
items.example: The contract defines Roblox as the corporate entities that provide the Services.

items.definition: Interfaces, graphics, avatars, trademarks, data, code, software, and other platform materials owned by Roblox, plus related intellectual property rights.
items.example: Copying official UI assets outside allowed tools can violate Roblox IP protections.

items.definition: The full package of rules covering User Terms, Creator Terms, Community Standards, privacy and cookie policies, regional add-ons, and Additional Terms.
items.example: The Roblox Terms link the rules that apply to users and creators.

items.definition: A narrow creator license allowing Roblox trademark use only with Virtual Content or experiences hosted on Roblox, not unrestricted branding rights.
items.example: The Roblox Trademark License does not let you put the logo on third-party merch.

items.definition: A Robloxian is a person who plays on Roblox, often used for the community as a whole or a player’s in-world identity.
items.example: Many Robloxians joined the experience launch party on day one.

items.definition: Robux is Roblox’s official virtual currency used to buy avatar items, game passes, developer products, and other in-experience purchases.
items.example: They saved Robux for a limited catalog item and a game pass on their favorite map.
items.safetyNote: Only spend Robux through official Roblox purchase flows, and never share account access or payment details with others.

items.definition: Roblox's split of Robux from a Virtual Content sale among the creator, any seller, and the platform according to current rules.
items.example: Marketplace sales show a Robux Allocation that leaves a platform fee after the creator share.

items.definition: A chat acronym meaning something is extremely funny.
items.example: The cart launched into the ceiling and the whole server typed ROFL.

items.definition: A named membership level in a Roblox Community that can carry its own permissions and responsibilities.
items.example: The event host role could post announcements but could not change the owner role.

items.definition: Roleplay is acting as a character or job inside an experience, following story, rules, and social cues instead of pure combat scores.
items.example: In the cafe game they roleplay as staff and guests instead of racing for points.

items.definition: Rthro was Roblox’s more human-proportioned avatar body style and scaling system introduced for modern character looks.
items.example: Older posts still call taller, more realistic body proportions Rthro even as avatar options keep changing.

items.definition: A Luau code container that commonly runs on the server and controls shared game logic.
items.example: The Script awarded the badge after the server confirmed the finish.

items.definition: In match slang, selling means playing so poorly that your team loses value or the round, not buying or trading items.
items.example: After three free goals, chat said the keeper was selling the ranked match.

items.definition: A running copy of a Roblox place where a group of players shares the same live session.
items.example: When one server filled up, the next players joined another copy of the same map.

items.definition: Server hop means leaving one live instance of an experience and joining another server, often to find a quieter lobby or different players.
items.example: They server hopped until they found a map with open trade booths and fewer people.

items.definition: Roblox websites, apps, Player, Studio, products, content, software, data feeds, and related offerings provided under the Roblox Terms.
items.example: Studio and the mobile client are both part of the Roblox Services.

items.definition: A formation command telling players to stand one behind another, often in military or training roleplay.
items.example: The trainer called SFL before leading the recruits through the course.

items.definition: An insult for an exploiter who uses scripts made by other people without understanding them.
items.example: The moderator called the cheater a skid, then reported the behavior instead of arguing.
items.safetyNote: Do not download or run exploit tools or copied scripts. They can break rules, steal accounts, or install malware.

items.definition: Roblox slang for a tall, thin avatar style built with body scaling, long limbs, and a recognizable outfit aesthetic.
items.example: The outfit guide used a slender avatar so the layered clothes had a taller silhouette.

items.definition: A chat reaction showing disappointment, disbelief, or mild annoyance.
items.example: He sold the quest item by mistake and typed SMH.

items.definition: A smurf is an alternate account, often used by an experienced player in lower-level or fresher lobbies than their main.
items.example: The new username played like a pro, so the lobby guessed it was a smurf.

items.definition: A widely recognized distress call used in Roblox survival, combat, and roleplay scenes to ask for urgent help.
items.example: SOS at the north tower, the boss trapped our squad.
items.safetyNote: Treat a real safety threat seriously. Use Roblox reporting tools and tell a trusted adult when appropriate.

items.definition: Spawn is the place a player appears when joining or returning after defeat, and the verb for that appearance.
items.example: The team met at spawn before walking to the first objective.

items.definition: Spawn kill means defeating players right as they appear at spawn, giving them little chance to move or fight back.
items.example: The lobby asked for fair play after repeated spawn kill rounds near the entry pad.

items.definition: Roleplay-community shorthand announcing that the current organized server session is ending.
items.example: The host posted SSD after the final training event.

items.definition: Roleplay-community shorthand announcing that an organized server session is opening or beginning.
items.example: The community posted SSU before members joined the roleplay server.

items.definition: The first place players load into when they join a Roblox game or experience.
items.example: The creator made the lobby the start place and teleported players to match maps from there.

items.definition: A formation command telling players to line up side by side, often in military or training roleplay.
items.example: The officer called STS so the squad formed one straight row.

items.definition: Studio is Roblox’s creation app for building experiences, scripting gameplay, testing places, and publishing to the platform.
items.example: They opened Studio to fix the door script and publish a small map update.

items.definition: The limited permission Roblox grants creators to install and use Roblox Studio for building and publishing content on the platform.
items.example: The Creator Terms describe the Studio License for using Roblox Studio.

items.definition: A purchase that renews on a schedule until it is canceled. Roblox games can use subscriptions for ongoing in-game benefits.
items.example: The player reviewed the renewal details before starting the game's subscription.
items.safetyNote: Review the current price, renewal period, and cancellation information before subscribing.

items.definition: A sweat is a player who tries extremely hard to win, using high effort, strong loadouts, and little room for casual play.
items.example: The casual server got quiet when a full sweat squad joined ranked voice chat.

items.definition: Chat slang for the hashtag symbols Roblox shows when part of a message is filtered.
items.example: Her sentence came out as tags, so she rewrote it in simpler, appropriate words.
items.safetyNote: Do not try to work around the chat filter. Rewrite the message safely or leave out private information.

items.definition: The middle tier of Roblox's retired Builders Club membership.
items.example: The old account comparison lists TBC between BC and OBC.

items.definition: A chat phrase used before a direct opinion or honest reaction.
items.example: TBH, the starter sword works better after the update.

items.definition: Roblox Studio collaboration that lets approved creators work in the same project.
items.example: The builders used Team Create to edit different rooms at the same time.
items.safetyNote: Give edit access only to collaborators you trust.

items.definition: A Roblox-owned starter resource for building UGC that creators may use under the Studio License when beginning new experiences or assets.
items.example: A creator can begin a project with a Template provided through Studio.

items.definition: Termed means a Roblox account was terminated, so the player can no longer use that account under normal access.
items.example: After repeated serious rule breaks, the old account was termed and stayed locked.
items.safetyNote: Treat termination as a serious account status. Keep play fair and report harmful behavior through official Roblox tools.

items.definition: An image applied to a 3D surface to add color, detail, or a material-like appearance.
items.example: The creator changed the crate texture without rebuilding its mesh.

items.definition: Outside content, tools, or materials offered through or alongside Roblox that Roblox does not own or control.
items.example: The Terms distinguish Third-Party Services from tools and content controlled by Roblox.

items.definition: Tix were Roblox’s old free tickets currency, removed years ago when the platform moved fully to Robux.
items.example: Veteran players still joke about buying hats with Tix before tickets left the platform.

items.definition: A Roblox Studio panel for finding and inserting Creator Store assets and a creator's own assets.
items.example: The builder opened Toolbox to find a tree model for the park.
items.safetyNote: Inspect inserted models and scripts before using them in a published game.

items.definition: An older Roblox discovery label for games ranked by how much Robux they generated during a period.
items.example: The archived homepage screenshot has a Top Earning chart beside the popular games.

items.definition: Trade is the official exchange of eligible avatar items or limiteds between players through Roblox’s trading features.
items.example: They opened a trade for two limiteds and waited for both sides to confirm.
items.safetyNote: Only trade through official Roblox trade windows. Never trust chat deals that ask you to leave the platform or share your password.

items.definition: A troll is someone who bothers others on purpose, such as spamming chat, ruining a roleplay, or blocking progress for attention.
items.example: The server muted the troll after they kept knocking builds over in the sandbox.
items.safetyNote: Do not join in. Leave, block, or report players who harass others, and keep your own chat respectful.

items.definition: TY is a short chat way to say thank you after help, a gift, a trade confirm, or a clutch play.
items.example: After the revive, they typed TY and followed the squad back to base.

items.definition: A quick chat shorthand for thanking someone a lot, often after a trade help, save, or kind reply.
items.example: Player: TYSM for showing me where the portal is!

items.definition: Content made by Roblox players and creators, including experiences, avatar items, models, clothing, and other community-built assets, not only official Roblox-made content.
items.example: That parkour map is popular UGC built by an independent studio on the platform.

items.definition: The rights users and creators grant Roblox to host, display, and otherwise use their UGC under the User Terms and Creator Terms.
items.example: Publishing an outfit grants Roblox a UGC License to show it on the marketplace.

items.definition: A renewable creator subscription purchased with real-world money that delivers ongoing benefits to subscribers under the creator's offer.
items.example: A creator's UGC Subscription may provide continuing benefits described in its offer.

items.definition: User-generated content or experiences that synchronize Licensed Music into the experience or asset under Roblox's music licensing rules.
items.example: An experience becomes UGC with Licensed Music when licensed audio is synchronized into it.

items.definition: The internal Roblox project container that groups a game or experience with its places and shared settings.
items.example: The lobby and battle maps belong to the same universe but use different places.

items.definition: Chat slang claiming an item was purchased with real money outside Roblox’s official systems. Such deals are unsafe and against platform rules, so treat the label as a warning sign rather than a normal shopping tip.
items.example: If someone brags that a limited is USD-bought, do not trust the offer and stay on official Roblox trades only.
items.safetyNote: Never buy or sell Roblox items for real money off the platform. Keep trades and purchases inside Roblox, ignore pressure to move chats elsewhere, and report suspicious sellers.

items.definition: Any person or organization that accesses or uses Roblox Services, whether as a player, creator, or other account holder.
items.example: Every User must follow the Community Standards while playing or publishing content.

items.definition: Personally identifiable information that belongs to a user, such as details that can identify them as an individual.
items.example: Support tickets should avoid sharing extra User PII beyond what staff need.

items.definition: The terms that apply to everyone using Roblox, covering accounts, purchases, trading, safety expectations, and core legal conditions.
items.example: Purchase refunds are handled under the User Terms purchase and payment sections.

items.definition: The unique name that identifies a Roblox account, separate from its changeable display name.
items.example: Two players shared a display name, so the moderator checked their usernames.
items.safetyNote: A username is public. Never share a password, recovery code, or login link with it.

items.definition: Roblox voice chat, where eligible players can talk with nearby or party members using a microphone instead of only typing.
items.example: I turned on VC so my friends could call out where the boss was spawning.
items.safetyNote: Only enable voice chat with people you trust, mute or leave if talk gets unkind, and never share personal details over audio.

items.definition: All Roblox-created content and UGC that users can acquire, including Virtual Items and In-Experience Items across the platform.
items.example: Clothing, accessories, and game passes all fall under Virtual Content in the Terms.

items.definition: Roblox-created or user-generated digital goods—such as avatar clothing and accessories—that users can acquire for use on avatars.
items.example: A new jacket listed on the marketplace is a Virtual Item for your avatar.

items.definition: In roleplay, voided means an action or scene is treated as if it did not happen, usually because it broke the server's roleplay rules.
items.example: The moderator voided the crash scene after a player ignored the server's roleplay rules.

items.definition: Chat slang for a win, good outcome, or praise. Players call a play, fit, or decision a W when they think it was solid.
items.example: That clutch save was a massive W for our team.

items.definition: A label for experiences, maps, models, or clothing still being built and not finished yet.
items.example: The creator tagged the new lobby as WIP, so only test systems were open.

items.definition: A text emoticon that looks like a big laughing face, used to show something is funny or silly in chat.
items.example: I fell off the tower right at the end XD
